newsitem.title: ITALY: Greek PM Simitis says Turkey aggressive in Aegean.
newsitem.headline: Greek PM Simitis says Turkey aggressive in Aegean.

text.p: Greek Prime Minister Costas Simitis accused Turkey on Tuesday of pursuing "a policy of aggression" in the Aegean region which he said violated international law.
Simitis, in a speech to an international gathering of Socialists, said Turkey was using its quarrels with Greece to deflect attention away from domestic troubles.

"Instead of concentrating on the serious internal problems of Turkish society...the Turkish government has embarked on a nationalistic policy towards Greece, disorientating their public opinion and citizens," he said.

Tensions between Greece and Turkey have risen sharply in recent weeks following an announcement by the Greek Cypriot government that it planned to buy and install a Russian anti-aircraft missile system.
Turkey has promised closer military and political links with the self-declared Turkish Cypriot republic in response to the Greek Cypriot plans.
Cyprus has been divided since Turkey invaded in 1974 in response to a Greek Cypriot coup backed by Athens.
Turkey, which keeps 30,000 soldiers on Cyprus, has threatened to use force to halt the missile deployment, which is due to take place in about 16 months.

"Turkey is following a policy of aggression and threats towards Greece in an effort to upset the existing status quo in the Aegean in defiance of international law and treaties," Simitis told delegates on Tuesday.

Simitis said Greece had asked Turkey to engage in "a step by step approach" to solve their differences on the basis of international law. "We hope that Turkey responds positively to our initiative," he added.
In Ankara, Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan told a meeting of his Islam-based Welfare Party on Tuesday that Turkey would not wait passively for the next 16 months.
Erbakan called on the Greek Cypriot administration, regarded internationally as the island's only government, to announce it will scrap the missile deal.
